analysis.title: Iran War Chartpack Week 34: (F)Lame Duck
key_insights: SEB sees the Middle East equilibrium as inherently unstable absent a diplomatic breakthrough. Concerns center on renewed fighting after the US midterms, and a poor Republican result may not reduce Trump's incentive for renewed conflict.

Reports of attempted Israeli renewal of attacks after the midterms, plus the risk of Iranian retaliation or preemption, point to a volatile last quarter of 2026. Heavy munitions are reportedly being discussed.
Iranian tanker attacks have become more numerous and severe and may intensify ahead of the US midterms. Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure show vulnerabilities beyond tanker transit.
Iran has shown it can withstand the blockade for several months. Some analysts believe the US Navy may have less than six months to hold an effective blockade of Iran in the Strait of Hormuz (SoH).

Trump's options are to continue the blockade, accept Iran's demands and reopen the SoH at a strategic cost, or intensify the war. SEB says acquiescence is unlikely because of domestic US political costs.
The Israeli election on Oct 27 creates escalation incentives. Election incentives tilt toward pro-war rhetoric, and Israel may have a higher risk tolerance than the US.
SEB's scenario table puts a 0.35 probability on renewed conflict (Brent $100-150) and 0.60 on prolonged conflict overall. Negotiation scenarios carry 0.35 and capitulation 0.05.
The scenario-weighted Brent price implied for 3 months is $99.0, against a current market price of $103.3.

EIA's STEO expects Brent to average $105/b in 4Q26 (up $14/b from last month's STEO) and $84/b next year. Middle East oil flows stay constrained through 4Q26, and most regional production is expected back to pre-conflict levels by the end of 2Q27.

Regional crude shut-ins averaged 4.8m b/d in September, down from 5.8m b/d in August and a 10.9m b/d peak in May. Global inventories fell 1.9m b/d in 3Q26 and are forecast to fall a further 0.7m b/d in 4Q26.

The gasoil-Brent crack spread rose from about $27/bbl at the start of 2025 to a peak of $101/bbl in September. SEB cites Iran War disruption, Ukrainian strikes on Russian diesel exports, limited European refining capacity and seasonal demand.
Physical and paper oil prices diverge. Sticky longer-dated divergence indicates the market is pricing supply pressure into 2027.

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalated, with 15-20 attack waves on six of seven days in early October. Targets included King Khalid International Airport and an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, and Saudi Arabia struck Houthi fuel infrastructure on Oct 13.

Houthi attacks and a declared blockade on Saudi-linked vessels make Bab al-Mandeb a second chokepoint and have reduced SoH traffic, putting upward pressure on oil prices. Trump says the US is evaluating whether to join Saudi Arabia's offensive.

Appendix material argues Iran is shifting toward offensive deterrence, citing WSJ and FT reports of possible sabotage of Gulf internet cables and strikes on US bases in Europe. The US is leaning on economic measures, including targeting Chinese banks and Hong Kong payment channels for Iranian oil.

US munitions depletion constrains further large campaigns. CSIS estimates Tomahawk, THAAD and Patriot inventories take 3+ years to restore, with Tomahawk back to prewar levels in late 2030 to early 2031.

Iran's economy is under severe strain. July headline inflation was 88% (food 128%), and the country is in its eighth currency crisis since 2016. Storage estimates of 20-35mb imply roughly 2-3 weeks before forced production cuts.

SEB's base case from its June note remains a 'skinny' deal deferring core disagreements, with tail risk of uncontrolled escalation. Sovereign CDS spreads are rising again, and the IMF October 2026 WEO shows large downward GDP revisions for MENA.

sector_views.rationale: SEB's scenario-weighted Brent is $99.0 versus $103.3 current, with renewed-conflict scenarios at $100-150 and EIA forecasting a 4Q26 average of $105.

macro_indicators.interpretation: $14/b above last month's STEO. EIA expects Brent to fall to an average of $84/b next year as Middle East production recovers.
Assumes most regional production returns to pre-conflict averages by end of 2Q27.
SEB's weighted average of scenario oil prices, not a forecast. It sits below the current market price of $103.3.
Current price is above the scenario-weighted implied price.
Down from 5.8m b/d in August and a 10.9m b/d peak in May, showing partial recovery.
EIA expects a further 0.7m b/d draw in 4Q26.
Up from about $27/bbl at the start of 2025, reflecting disrupted product flows and limited European refining capacity.
Record-high inflation alongside a falling currency adds economic pressure on the regime.

risk_factors: Renewed US/Israeli-Iran fighting after the midterms, with reports of very heavy munitions being discussed and the risk of mutually assured energy destruction.
Escalation around the Israeli Oct 27 election and the new US Congress seated in January 2027.
Wider regional war hitting energy, water and undersea cable infrastructure.
Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and aviation, and a second chokepoint at Bab al-Mandeb.
Iranian tanker attacks intensifying ahead of the US midterms.
Persistent diesel and product price pressure, supply chain disruption and cost-push energy inflation.
Rising sovereign credit risk, shown in higher CDS spreads.
Depleted US interceptor and standoff munitions stocks limiting escalation options.
charts_described: Table of scenario probabilities and Brent prices shows scenario-weighted implied Brent at $99.0 against $103.3 market.
Munitions table lists CSIS estimates of return to prewar inventory, for example Tomahawk in late 2030 to early 2031 and PrSM in late 2026.
vol_and_positioning: Physical and paper oil prices diverge, and sticky longer-dated divergence indicates supply pressure priced into 2027.
The gasoil-Brent crack spread peaked at $101/bbl in September.
geopolitical: Possible renewed US/Israeli fighting with Iran after the US midterms, with Iranian retaliation or preemption risk.
US naval blockade of Iran and Iranian restrictions at the Strait of Hormuz, with SEB citing less than six months of blockade capacity per some analysts.
Israeli election on Oct 27 raising escalation incentives.
Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh, KKIA and an Aramco building in Dhahran, and Saudi strikes on Houthi fuel infrastructure on Oct 13.
Houthi declared blockade on Saudi-linked vessels at Bab al-Mandeb, and Trump evaluating whether to join the Saudi offensive.
Houthi encirclement of Taiz City as of Oct 12, with possible advance on Aden.
Reported Iranian shift toward offensive deterrence, including possible sabotage of Gulf internet cables and strikes on US bases in Europe.
Planned new US economic pressure on Iranian oil financing, including Chinese banks and Hong Kong.
Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader since March 2026, with uncertainty over whether he is alive and IRGC influence expanding.
US munitions depletion and damage to US Middle East bases from Iranian strikes.

tension_points.bull_case: A diplomatic opening or skinny deal could ease Strait of Hormuz disruption, and SEB assigns 0.35 probability to negotiation scenarios.
tension_points.bear_case: Renewed conflict, assigned 0.35 probability with Brent at $100-150, driven by Israeli election incentives, Iranian preemption and depleted US munitions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A durable diplomatic breakthrough would invalidate the escalation case, and renewed post-midterm strikes would invalidate the negotiation case.

theme_stances.key_argument: The current equilibrium is unstable absent a diplomatic breakthrough, and the road to intensified conflict remains open.
theme_stances.evidence: the prevailing geopolitical equilibrium in the Middle East is inherently unstable

theme_stances.evidence: market is pricing in supply pressure into 2027
